clue.text: Highland service provided carnet for exchange student

indicators.note: letters offered for exchange are swapped around into a fresh order

blocks.note: a Mass is a church service
provided that = if
the six letters of carnet, rearranged
L for learner, the usual crossword student

explanation.surface: A travel permit swapped by a foreign student enables a service in some mountain region.
explanation.walkthrough: MASS + IF + CENTRA + L. A carnet is a customs or travel document. 'Provided' is wordplay, giving IF, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massif Central is the great upland plateau of south-central France, a highland area.

clue.text: One has ice cream prepared in a dish

indicators.note: prepared suggests ingredients being worked up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone eats ice cream served in a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' hints at dessert, but the answer is a savoury pasta bake.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni cheese is a baked pasta dish in cheese sauce, known in the US as mac and cheese.

clue.text: Bank starts to suspend card and refuse payment

indicators.note: the starts of the next several words are kept, their opening letters

blocks.note: opening letters of suspend, card, and, refuse, payment

explanation.surface: A bank stops a customer's card and refuses to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks financial but is a slope of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarp is a steep slope or escarpment, the same sense as a bank of earth.

clue.text: Immune to influence, Victor props up dodgy prime debt instruments

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order
in a down entry whatever props something up sits directly beneath it

blocks.note: the letters of prime rearranged
Victor is V in the NATO alphabet; it props up, so sits beneath, in a down entry
IOUs are written acknowledgments of debt

explanation.surface: An unmoved financier named Victor shores up shady prime loans.
explanation.definitionFit: Impervious means not affected or swayed by something, unmoved by pressure or persuasion.

clue.text: Mama who sang clubs wearing fine, long robe

indicators.note: something wearing a garment is inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Mama Cass Elliot of the Mamas and the Papas
OK = fine
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: A singing mother in clubwear puts on a fine long gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassock is the full-length garment worn by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: Unspoilt ancient city in old SA province

indicators.note: in places the city inside the province name

blocks.note: Natal was a South African province until 1994
Ur is the crossword's favourite ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: An unspoilt ancient city lies within a former South African province.
explanation.definitionFit: Something natural is untouched by human intervention, pure and unaltered.

clue.text: Criminal’s caught out swindler

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a crook is a criminal
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A criminal has been caught out by a con artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to cheat them, so a rook is a cheat or sharper, a con man.

clue.text: English soccer team at home in The Den?

blocks.note: first meaning: the England women's national football side
second, cryptic meaning: female big cats living in a lair, with a nod to Millwall's stadium, The Den

explanation.surface: An English football team plays a home game at Millwall's ground, The Den.
explanation.walkthrough: The Den is Millwall FC's London stadium, but the setter means a lair where female big cats live.
explanation.definitionFit: The England women's football team is nicknamed the Lionesses, after the three lions on the badge.

clue.text: Wearing kit, Italian club set to play Partisan side

indicators.note: to play with something is to move it about, so the letters change their order

blocks.note: vested = dressed, in vestments
Inter Milan, the Italian football club
the letters of set rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian football club in its kit is ready to face a partisan team.
explanation.definitionFit: A vested interest is a personal stake that makes someone biased, the partisan side of a matter.

clue.text: Tool for gripping shellfish, pointed at the front

indicators.note: only what stands at the front of the word is kept, its opening letter

blocks.note: a clam is a bivalve shellfish
the opening letter of pointed

explanation.surface: A description of some implement for picking up shellfish with a sharp tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a device that holds things tightly together, a gripping tool for workshops.

clue.text: Undertones performed like this – drunk, one failing to sing?

blocks.note: surface reading: The Undertones, a Northern Irish punk band, giving a gig
setter's reading: tones kept under, as a mumbling drunk who cannot manage a song might murmur the words

explanation.surface: A tipsy fan at a gig by the Undertones fails to sing along.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Undertones' as tones kept under, i.e. very quiet utterance; the drunk who cannot sing just murmurs, and the Italian phrase also suggests a SOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction means in an undertone, quietly, literally beneath the voice, so it is how hushed tones are delivered.

clue.text: Note bold soirée uncovered everything for performance

indicators.note: with its covering stripped off, the word loses its outside letters and only the inner part is kept

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
pert means cheeky or bold
soirée without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone at an evening party behaves cheekily and bares all for a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A repertoire is the whole stock of pieces a performer or company is ready to present.

clue.text: Resigned from the French newspaper

blocks.note: le is a French word for the
FT is the Financial Times, a London newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone stepped down from a French newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To have left a job is to have quit or walked away from it, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Yes, heartless blond Conservative admits “made up fantasy”

indicators.note: with the heart gone only the outside letters are kept
to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: fair = light-haired
yes without its middle letter
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A blond Tory politician concedes that a claim was invented.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy story is a fanciful tale, and by extension an invented, untrue account.

clue.text: Back in Birmingham’s first beat club

indicators.note: back tells us to read the following short word from its end to its start
first asks for only the initial letter of the city name

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
the opening letter of Birmingham
to lick is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Someone is back in Birmingham, having beaten the city's top club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a football side but is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old-fashioned iron golf club, roughly a modern nine-iron.

clue.text: Song from pub singer King famously

blocks.note: bar = pub
Carole King, the American singer-songwriter

explanation.surface: A famous singer named King performs a song in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a Venetian gondolier's boat song, or a piece written in that rhythm.

clue.text: Told fibs about first-class head of state that’s acted as intermediary

indicators.note: about places the lying word around everything that follows
head of picks out just the top, initial letter

blocks.note: lied = told fibs
A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I
the opening letter of state

explanation.surface: A diplomat told fibs about a top-ranking head of state while brokering talks.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to act as a link or go-between, so the past tense fits acting as intermediary.

clue.text: Endless merry-go-round of US party

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: an American word for a merry-go-round

explanation.surface: A never-ending round of American parties.
explanation.walkthrough: CAROUSEL without its L. Americans say carousel where the British say merry-go-round.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and make merry noisily, so it works as the verb party.

clue.text: Having a job, longing to spend yen

indicators.note: what is spent is used up and gone, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: yearning = longing
Y is the abbreviation for yen, Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Someone in work yearns to splash out in Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone earning is drawing a wage, so is employed.

clue.text: Comedy act, very new, excites

blocks.note: a turn is a performer's act in a variety show
so = very
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A very new comedy routine thrills its audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone on is to arouse or stimulate them, an idiom for exciting.

clue.text: Conference side failing to finish attack

indicators.note: not finishing means the final letter is missing

blocks.note: a side is a team
to chin someone is to punch them on the chin

explanation.surface: A team fails to complete an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an extended meeting of lectures and discussions on one topic, a kind of conference.

clue.text: Hairy chap selecting news value periodically?

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of news value

explanation.surface: Someone shaggy weighs how often the news is worth reading.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Esau was born hairy, unlike his smooth twin Jacob.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible describes Esau as a hairy man, so he is the archetypal hairy biblical figure.

clue.text: Bachelor studies brilliant, featuring university accompaniment to main course

indicators.note: featuring means including something within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor
to read a subject is to study it
ace = brilliant
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A student's brilliant work at university is praised alongside a main course.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread sauce is a thick milky sauce served with roast poultry, a traditional British side for Christmas dinner.

clue.text: Peacekeepers fight to get out?

blocks.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers fight to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: to unbox is to get something out of its packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbox is to take a product from its packaging, literally getting the contents out.

clue.text: Move gradually along ridge, letting go of line

indicators.note: letting go of something means releasing it, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a ledge is a narrow ridge or shelf
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A climber shuffles along a ridge after releasing the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge along is to creep forward slowly and carefully, inching sideways.

clue.text: One swimming in lochs if drowsy must turn around

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows
turning around means the concealed letters are read back to front

blocks.note: letters running across lochs, if and drowsy

explanation.surface: A sleepy creature drifts around in Scottish lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The swordfish is a large ocean fish, so it is one that swims, a vague but fair description.

clue.text: Header disallowed in dismal game featuring dozens of cards

indicators.note: the head is not allowed, so the opening letter is cut off

blocks.note: sombre = gloomy, dismal

explanation.surface: A football header is ruled out in a dreary match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Header disallowed' sounds like a refereeing call but means lose the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is an old three-player card game popular in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, played with a forty-card pack.

clue.text: Greece: my next island hopping escape

indicators.note: hopping about suggests the letters jump around into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An island-hopping tourist plans the next getaway from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency exit is a door used for getting out quickly in danger, so it is a means of escape.
